purpose: Maps every row of scripts/frontend-migration.json to the React-side proof that stands for it, so the default can change only over a complete, named parity suite.
scope: The checker proves that each named proof exists (the test file and the title or browser step it names) and that no inventory row is unmapped. It does not judge that a proof covers its contract; that judgement is the reviewer's, row by row, and each mapping was chosen against the row's contract text.

status_meanings.proven: A React-side proof exists and is named.
status_meanings.deviation: Proven, with a difference from the legacy page recorded in the design record paragraph the entry links.
status_meanings.deferred: Owned by a named later issue; carries a reason.
status_meanings.gap: No React-side proof was found for something the contract or the column asks for; recorded plainly for the lead.

production_artifact.limits: The Python backend serves the React side without Vite in production mode. Served the tracked minified react.html itself (no scratch copy, no mutation): the shell, sessions, intent, drift, project, attention, console, capacity, and terminal and timeline proofs. Each drives its surface through the shipped page's own mount point (the strip in the Sessions view, the consent and observer controls and the terminal in the Console tab, the timeline in the Decisions tab), and a `shipped page` step in the capacity proof fails if the strip or the consent is not inside its view. A mutation run is served a production build of a scratch copy made by the same packaging code. Still harness-hosted, because the shipped page cannot reach them with a fixture: the controls proof mounts the controls gallery, which composes combinations of the shared controls (a stack of draft fields, selects and disclosures, composition and undo cases) that no one project or session page draws together, so those controls are proven in the shipped composition only through the sessions, project, intent, drift, attention and shell proofs, not by the gallery's own cases; and the storage proof's React side is the storage codec bundled minified in the browser, not a served page. On the shipped page three harness-only readings are replaced by what a reader can observe, and the proofs say so where they do it: the terminal owner's internal counters become the renderer count and the open terminal sockets (the owner's last-opened key is asserted only in development), the console's accepted-board count becomes the count of board answers, and a manual refresh becomes another tab's revision announcement. StrictMode double effects exist only in development, so the production run proves the same counts without the double mount, and the development run of every proof stays in CI.
